spec_features.spec_quote: Default max turns per task = 20 (not 10, not 30)
spec_features.evidence: eval_harness.py:356 default `max_turns: int = 20`; enforced in process_turn at line 372-373 (`if len(self.execution.turns) >= self.max_turns: return "Max turns reached", False`) and line 412 (`should_continue = not success and turn_num < self.max_turns`). Runner wires it: eval_runner.py:46 `max_turns_per_task: int = 20`, passed at :229 to TaskHarness, and the loop breaks on should_continue (eval_runner.py:241-243; also integration_examples.py:161-170). The cap is checked and actually ends the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuine end-to-end hard cap on how many failure turns the subject endures. Bounds the experiment per task.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Consider reducing max_turns from {self.config.max_turns_per_task}. (eval_runner.py:376, under '# Cost optimization')

spec_features.spec_quote: Early Stopping: Could theoretically stop early once degradation clear (future feature)
spec_features.evidence: Spec itself labels it a '(future feature)' (DESIGN.md:486). In code, `early_stop_saturated: bool = True` is only a config field (eval_runner.py:52) set again at :481, but grep shows it is never read in any branch (`grep -rn early_stop|saturat|plateau /codebase/*.py` returns only the comment line 15, the field def line 52, and its setter line 481). Degradation severity is computed (eval_harness.py:602-606) but never compared to a threshold to stop the loop; the only stop conditions are success or max_turns (eval_harness.py:412).
spec_features.notes: Unused config flag and a discarded severity value; no code path acts on either to stop early.
